item.title: PEI 2025-2026 Public Accounts show improvement in deficit, increased revenues
item.description:
PEI 2025-2026 Public Accounts show improvement in deficit, increased revenues jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/02/2026 - 16:04

Today, the Government of PEI released all three volumes of the 2025-2026 Public Accounts showing its audited financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026.

The 2025-2026 fiscal year ended with a deficit of $355.5 million. This was $94.1 million lower than forecast in spring 2026, as part of the operating budget estimates. 

“Islanders expect us to manage the finances responsibly and these Public Accounts demonstrate that we are taking action on responsible fiscal management. Our strong economy has helped increase revenues, and we’re within our target fiscal anchors. We’re positioning our province for sustainable future growth while continuing to invest in what matters most to Islanders.”

- Minister of Finance and Affordability Jill Burridge

Revenues for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, were just over $3.3 billion. This is $192.7 million higher than in 2024-25 and $45.5 million above the 2026 spring forecast. The increase from spring 2026 forecast was mainly due to higher than anticipated provincial corporate tax revenue.

Expenditures for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, were just over $3.6 billion. Key areas of expenditure include:

  • $1.4 billion in Health and Wellness and Health PEI
  • $475.2 million in Education and Early Years
  • $232.0 million in Social Development and Seniors
  • $223.1 million in Transportation and Infrastructure
  • $200.8 million in Workforce, Advanced Learning and Population

Net debt at March 31, 2026, was $3.7 billion, or 32.3 per cent of GDP, reflecting strong ongoing investments in tangible capital assets. 

Public Accounts is an annual financial summary and accountability report of the Government of Prince Edward Island, audited by the Auditor General. 

For more information on public accounts, visit Public Accounts | Government of Prince Edward Island.

item.title: Older adults recognized with Senior Islander of the Year Award
item.description:
Older adults recognized with Senior Islander of the Year Award jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/02/2026 - 15:01

Nine Islanders were honoured today with the 2026 Senior Islander of the Year Award for their lasting impact on communities across Prince Edward Island.

The award promotes positive images of aging and celebrates the many contributions of PEI residents who are 65 years and older. This year’s and past recipients have been recognized for a variety of efforts, including community activities and engagement, volunteering, fundraising, education, research, fitness and recreation. 

“Congratulations to all the winners of the 2026 Senior Islander of the Year award. Receiving this award is a significant honour. Your dedication, compassion, and community spirit have touched the lives of many Islanders. We are grateful for your contributions and proud to celebrate your accomplishments.”

- Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay

The winners of the 2026 award are:

  • Carol White (Murray Harbour) 
  • Hu Meihua (Stratford) 
  • Kaye Morrison (Charlottetown)
  • Miriam Lank (Meadowbank) 
  • Georgie Smith (Kinkora)
  • Carol MacLean (Summerside)
  • Doug Bryson (Union Corner) 
  • Claude Blaquière (Mont-Carmel)
  • Beverley Ann Boulter (O’Leary)

“The older adults we are recognizing today have demonstrated an exceptional commitment to their communities,” said chair of the PEI Seniors’ Secretariat Peter Holman. “Through their leadership, generosity, and dedication, they have created lasting positive change and strengthened the communities they serve. It is a privilege to celebrate and recognize their achievements, and to thank them for making our province a better place.”

To learn more, visit Senior Islander of the Year Award.

item.title: New accessible taxi ready to serve
item.description:
New accessible taxi ready to serve jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/02/2026 - 14:24

A new accessible transportation service, Cudmore’s Accessible Cab, is now available for residents and visitors with disabilities across Charlottetown, Stratford, and Cornwall.

Cudmore’s Accessible Cab is a two-year pilot project operated by Pat & the Elephant. The cab is an on-demand, first-come, first-serve taxi service that provides spontaneous and safe transportation throughout the capital region. The cab is named after Paul Cudmore, a long-time advocate for Islanders with disabilities.

The pilot project is funded through a partnership between the Government of Prince Edward Island, the City of Charlottetown, the Town of Stratford, and the Town of Cornwall.

Service is available daily from 7 a.m. to 1 a.m., Sunday through Thursday. On Fridays and Saturdays, hours are extended from 7 a.m. to 3 a.m. Fares start at $8.50 plus $1.60 per kilometer. There are no additional charges for extra passengers or waiting time. The service can accommodate up to two wheelchairs at a time. 

No advance booking is required. To book a ride, call (782) 377-8416. The service accepts cash or debit. Credit cards are not accepted at this time. 

Cudmore’s Accessible Cab is supported by a committee that includes representatives from Pat & The Elephant, the Department of Social Development and Seniors, the City of Charlottetown, the Towns of Stratford and Cornwall, ResourceAbilities and the PEI Spinal Cord Injury Association.

To learn more visit Cudmore’s Cab — Accessible On-Demand Taxi, PEI Capital Region 

Quotes:

“Making this service a reality has been a true team effort and I’m proud of what we have accomplished together. Cudmore’s Accessible Cab will make a meaningful difference in people’s daily lives. This is an important step toward creating more inclusive communities and shows what can be achieved when governments and community partners work together to improve accessibility for Islanders.”

- Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay

“Accessible transportation is about independence, inclusion and being able to fully participate in community life. This new service will give people with disabilities more flexibility to get to work, attend appointments and activities, visit family and friends, or simply get where they need to go without having to plan every trip in advance. We are very excited to see this project come to fruition and to partner on an initiative that helps make Charlottetown and the capital region more accessible for everyone.”

- Mayor of Charlottetown Philip Brown

“The Town of Cornwall is proud to have been a part of the collaborative efforts that have brought this project into the reality of Cudmore’s Accessible Cab. This initiative will make it easier for Islanders to get around by removing travel barriers, making the Island more inclusive.”

- Mayor of Cornwall Minerva McCourt

“The Town of Stratford is a proud partner in this project. We know we have residents that will directly benefit from this much-needed service, allowing them to participate and attend events and activities that fall outside of the existing hours of service provided. We are pleased to be working alongside all partners to recognize and support this needed service that is now available.”

- Mayor of Stratford Steve Ogden

“At Pat & The Elephant, we believe transportation should never be a barrier to participating in community life. Cudmore’s Accessible Cab is an important step toward providing residents and visitors with disabilities the freedom to travel safely, spontaneously, and with dignity throughout the capital region. We are proud to partner with government, municipalities, and community organizations to deliver a service that helps make our communities more accessible and inclusive for everyone.”

- President of Pat & the Elephant Steve Brosseau

“We’re excited to have worked alongside a committee that has remained so passionate about bringing Cudmore’s Accessible Cab to life. Accessible transportation gives people with disabilities more freedom and flexibility to make plans, be spontaneous and participate fully in their communities.”

- Executive Director of ResourceAbilities Devon Broome

“Spinal Cord injury PEI is excited about the accessible cab and the work that has gone into making it a reality. We have been working at this for some time now amongst our own organization and in this collaborative effort.”

- Executive Director of Spinal Cord Injury PEI Glen Flood

item.title: Helping Islanders save millions on prescription drugs
item.description:
Helping Islanders save millions on prescription drugs jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/02/2026 - 11:28

As populations and the cost of drugs continue to grow, the Government of Canada and Prince Edward Island (PEI) are working together to make it easier for Islanders to access the prescription medications they need, while helping to reduce the cost of living. 

Today, the Honourable Heath MacDonald, Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food, on behalf of the Honourable Marjorie Michel, Canada’s Minister of Health, the Honourable Premier of PEI, Rob Lantz, and the Honourable Cory Deagle, Minister of Health and Wellness for PEI, announced the government intention to invest over $32 million over three years to support the Improving Affordable Access to Prescription Drugs Program (IAAPD) in PEI. 

The IAAPD program, launched in 2021, has funded targeted reforms to PEI’s public drug programs. PEI received $35 million (2021-22 to 2025-26) to expand its public formulary (list of publicly covered drugs) to broaden treatment options for Islanders and better align with public drug plans in other provinces and territories, lower out-of-pocket costs for residents, and gather insights and lessons learned. As of March 2025, the IAAPD has saved Islanders $13.8 million.

Extending the IAAPD will  allow PEI to maintain the improvements it has made to its public drug coverage system and help reduce the cost of living for its residents. 

Quotes

"We are working with PEI to make prescription drugs more affordable for Islanders. This renewed federal funding will help PEI maintain improvements to its public drug coverage and continue delivering savings for Islanders.”

The Honourable Marjorie Michel
Minister of Health

“Whether it is making prescription drugs more affordable, supporting finding a home, or helping local businesses grow, our government is focused on making investments that deliver for Islanders and strengthen communities across Prince Edward Island. I’m proud to see Islanders benefit from programs like this, which are putting money back in people’s pockets and helping make life more affordable for families across our province.”

The Honourable Heath MacDonald
Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food, Member of Parliament for Malpeque

"The renewal of this agreement reflects our commitment to making prescription medications more affordable and accessible for Islanders. By continuing this partnership, we are helping Islanders access the medications they need, strengthening our health-care system, and putting more money back into the pockets of Islanders." 

-The Honourable Rob Lantz
Premier of Prince Edward Island

“This program has made a real difference for Islanders, helping people access the medications they need to manage their health and well-being. For Islanders, this renewal means lower drug costs, access to more medications and fewer barriers to getting the treatment they need.”

The Honourable Cory Deagle
Minister of Health and Wellness, Government of Prince Edward Island

Quick Facts

  • Since its launch in 2021, the IAAPD has helped the province expand its formulary (list of covered drugs) to broaden treatment options for Islanders to a level of coverage more comparable with other provinces and territories and improve the affordability of its drug plans (e.g., by lowering out-of-pocket payments for residents).
  • Through IAAPD, PEI has made coverage improvements for Islanders, including: 
  • Expanded access to more than 100 medications, such as treatments for cancer and heart disease. 
  • Reduction of copays for commonly used cardiovascular, diabetes and mental health drugs, saving residents more than $9 million, with approximately 70% of these savings benefitting seniors. 
  • Delivery of no-cost treatment for alcohol and opioid use disorders to more than 1,200 Islanders through the Substance Use and Harm Reduction program. 
  • Expansion of the province's Community Mental Health Program to provide no-cost coverage of newer second-generation antipsychotic medications to long-term psychiatric patients.

item.title: Haunting season at PEI heritage sites
item.description:
Haunting season at PEI heritage sites jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/02/2026 - 10:34

The PEI Museum and Heritage Foundation invites Island residents and visitors to take part in seasonal events at Beaconsfield Historic House and Orwell Corner Historic Village.

The two sites will host the following events throughout October:

Beaconsfield by Candlelight – Beaconsfield Historic House

Experience Beaconsfield Historic House as the sun goes down and the shadows grow long. Hear local tales of 19th century true crime, meet the PEI Museum and Heritage Foundation's most haunted artifact, Wheelie, and peer into Beaconsfield Historic House's darkest corners.

Buy tickets online at Beaconsfield by Candlelight
 

Showtime is 5:30 p.m. - 6:30 p.m. (doors open at 5 p.m.)

Available dates: 

  • October 16, 17, 20, 23, 24, 27 and 30
  • November 3, 6, 7, 10, and 13 (Friday the 13th!)

Kids’ Halloween Hauntacular – Orwell Corner Historic Village

A family-friendly afternoon of Halloween fun, featuring trick-or-treating amongst the historic buildings, hands-on magic potion classes, wagon rides, blacksmithing demonstrations, family-friendly games, a village-wide scavenger hunt, and more!

Sunday, October 25 from 1pm to 3pm 

Buy tickets online at Kids’ Halloween Hauntacular  

“These events bring together elements of history, theatre, and Halloween magic,” said Matthew McRae, executive director, PEI Museum and Heritage Foundation. “From haunted evenings with a true crime twist at Beaconsfield, to family fun at Orwell Corner, we’re glad to offer something for everyone to enjoy this season.”

For more information about events, tickets, and programs call 902-368-6600 or visit https://www.peimuseum.ca/. Follow the Foundation on social media at @heritagepei.

item.title: Home heating program applications available through Access PEI this fall
item.description:
Home heating program applications available through Access PEI this fall jenniferdhogan Thu, 10/01/2026 - 15:38

Beginning November 1, eligible low-income Islanders can apply for support through the PEI Home Heating Program at any Access PEI location, providing easier access through more locations, online applications, and French-language services. 

Currently, the program is delivered by The Salvation Army and funded by the province. The Salvation Army will continue accepting applications until October 31. 

On November 1, Access PEI will start to administer the program and process all applications. Program eligibility and benefits remain unchanged, with eligible households able to receive up to $1,200 per calendar year.

The Province of Prince Edward Island thanks the Salvation Army for its contributions to administering the PEI Home Heating Program and for its dedicated service to Islanders.

For more information, visit PrinceEdwardIsland.ca/HomeHeatingProgram
